paragraphs: Bilevel optimization links two optimization problems, so decisions at one level depend on the solution of another. This paper addresses the pessimistic version, an area where efficient numerical methods are less developed than for optimistic formulations. Its specific goal is a gradient algorithm that avoids expensive derivative calculations and repeated inner optimization.

The authors first construct a smooth approximation using penalties and regularization. This approximation supplies the foundation for SiPBA, their Single-loop Pessimistic Bilevel Algorithm. SiPBA uses first-order gradient information and does not require an inner loop to solve subproblems. These design choices directly address two computational complications that can make bilevel algorithms cumbersome.

The paper provides theoretical support for the approximation and establishes convergence of SiPBA. Experiments on synthetic examples and practical applications also demonstrate effectiveness and efficiency. Together, these contributions connect a mathematically justified reformulation with a simpler computational procedure, giving pessimistic bilevel optimization a method specifically designed around a single loop of gradient updates.
neurips-2025-a-single-loop-gradient-algo.tldr: SiPBA uses a theoretically supported smooth approximation to solve pessimistic bilevel problems with a single-loop, first-order gradient algorithm.

paragraphs: The learning rate controls the size of each stochastic gradient descent update. Much existing theory studies rates that decrease according to a polynomial schedule, because these support attractive statistical guarantees. The paper identifies a practical mismatch: such schedules can converge prohibitively slowly, while schedules commonly used in practice have received less complete theoretical treatment.

The authors introduce a unified framework for quantifying uncertainty in online SGD under arbitrary learning-rate choices. They use it to characterize convergence for cyclical schedules and schedules that decay linearly to zero. This shifts the analysis from one familiar mathematical family toward a framework that can accommodate substantially different ways of changing update sizes.

The results are intended both to explain observed behavior and to support statistical inference and algorithm design. Extensive simulations across diverse settings corroborate the theoretical findings. The contribution is therefore a broader foundation for reasoning about SGD uncertainty and convergence, rather than a proposal that practitioners must adopt one particular learning-rate schedule.
neurips-2025-asymptotic-theory-of-sgd-wi.tldr: A unified theory characterizes online SGD uncertainty under general learning rates, including cyclical schedules and linear decay to zero.

paragraphs: A backdoored language model can respond to a carefully chosen input trigger by producing an attacker’s desired output. BackdoorLLM addresses the evaluation of these threats in open-ended text generation, where prior work is less developed than in vision and classification. Its central contribution is shared infrastructure for studying attacks and defenses systematically.

The benchmark combines a unified repository with standardized training and evaluation procedures. Its attack coverage includes poisoned training data, altered model weights, hidden-state manipulation, and chain-of-thought hijacking. More than 200 experiments span eight attack strategies, seven real-world scenarios, and six model architectures, allowing investigation across several different ways a backdoor can be introduced.

BackdoorLLM also includes seven representative mitigation techniques and reports insights into factors affecting attack effectiveness and failure. This makes it a resource for examining both vulnerabilities and responses within a common evaluation framework. The released code and datasets support further research, and the authors plan to incorporate emerging attack and defense methods as the area develops.
neurips-2025-backdoorllm-a-comprehensive.tldr: BackdoorLLM standardizes evaluation of language-model backdoors and defenses across diverse attacks, scenarios, and model architectures.

paragraphs: Contrastive learning trains representations by bringing matching examples together and separating nonmatching ones. Other examples in a training batch often supply the negatives, making batch composition important alongside batch size. B3 asks whether carefully selecting those examples can provide stronger training signals without requiring very large batches.

The method uses a pretrained teacher embedding model to rank dataset examples by similarity, then builds a sparse similarity graph. Community detection finds groups whose members can serve as challenging negatives for one another. These groups guide batch construction, concentrating useful comparisons into each batch instead of relying on size alone to provide them.

On the 36-task MMEB benchmark, B3 improves on previous best results by 1.3 points at the 7B scale and 2.9 points at the 2B scale. It surpasses existing state-of-the-art results with batches of 64, four to sixteen times smaller than those required by other methods. Additional experiments report generalization across domains and tasks, including strong performance with considerably weaker teachers.
neurips-2025-breaking-the-batch-barrier-.tldr: B3 uses teacher-guided similarity groups to build informative contrastive-learning batches, achieving stronger results with substantially smaller batches.

paragraphs: Keeping many fine-tuned models can require substantial storage even when they share a pretrained starting point. Delta compression instead stores that shared model plus compressed differences for each fine-tuned version. UltraDelta targets the difficulty of compressing those differences aggressively while preserving performance, using a pipeline that does not require data.

Its three components address different levels of information loss. Variance-based allocation retains more weights in high-variance layers. Distribution-aware compression quantizes values, groups similar parameters, and prunes within those groups to better preserve their distribution. Finally, trace-norm-guided rescaling estimates a global adjustment intended to stabilize the compressed model’s behavior.

Experiments report compression of up to 50 times for the tested LLaMA-2 fine-tunes, 224 times for general NLP models, 132 times for vision models, and 18 times for BEiT-3. UltraDelta consistently outperforms existing methods in these evaluations, particularly at very high compression. These results support coordinating decisions across layers, within layers, and globally when compressing the changes introduced by fine-tuning.
neurips-2025-breaking-the-compression-ce.tldr: UltraDelta compresses fine-tuning weight differences without data by coordinating sparsity, quantization, pruning, and global rescaling.

paragraphs: Object detectors with very large category vocabularies face an imbalance in their learning signals. Rare positive categories may receive too little emphasis, while numerous easy negatives can overwhelm the difficult distinctions the model needs to learn. CQ-DINO identifies these as two forms of gradient dilution and changes how category recognition is organized.

The framework replaces conventional classification with contrastive matching between object queries and learnable category queries. An image-guided selection mechanism uses cross-attention to retrieve the top-K relevant categories for each image. Reducing the negative candidate space rebalances training gradients and implicitly concentrates learning on harder examples. Category relationships are incorporated through explicit hierarchies or learned through self-attention.

On V3Det, CQ-DINO exceeds previous methods by a reported 2.1% AP while remaining competitive on COCO. The results support selecting relevant category comparisons as a way to improve detection with broad vocabularies. Its ability to use either supplied category structure or learned correlations also makes the approach applicable to the different dataset organizations examined in the paper.
neurips-2025-cq-dino-mitigating-gradient.tldr: CQ-DINO improves large-vocabulary detection by matching objects to category queries and selecting image-relevant categories to reduce gradient dilution.

paragraphs: When a transformer implements a graph algorithm, model size involves both depth and embedding width. Previous work showed that logarithmic depth can suffice when width grows sublinearly. This paper studies a different allocation of resources: allowing width to grow linearly while keeping the number of layers fixed as the problem grows.

The theoretical results show that linear width and constant depth suffice for a range of graph problems. Other problems require quadratic width. This distinction matters because it shows that replacing depth with width depends on the task; one architectural tradeoff does not describe every graph computation. The results map out several different possibilities for implementing these algorithms.

The authors also investigate the tradeoffs empirically. They identify tasks where wider models match deeper models’ accuracy while training and running much faster on parallelizable hardware. These experiments connect representational results to practical computation: a shallower architecture can be advantageous when its extra width is sufficient for the task and the hardware can exploit that width.
neurips-2025-depth-width-tradeoffs-for-t.tldr: For several graph tasks, linear transformer width permits constant depth, while other tasks require quadratic width.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary detectors can use text prompts to recognize categories beyond a fixed label list. They still benefit from adaptation for rare classes and specialized domains. DitHub addresses how to organize that adaptation when a detector needs multiple kinds of expertise, making a collection of specialist modules the central unit of the framework.

The design borrows the branch-and-merge idea from version control. Efficient adaptation modules are maintained as expert branches that can be fetched and merged when needed. This provides a concrete way to manage specialized knowledge and investigate its composition. The paper uses the framework to study how adaptation modules combine in object detection.

DitHub achieves state-of-the-art performance on ODinW-13 and on ODinW-O, a new benchmark introduced to assess class reappearance. The findings support modular adaptation as an effective approach in the evaluated incremental detection settings. Its broader contribution is to make the maintenance and combination of detector expertise an explicit part of the learning framework, alongside the quality of individual adaptations.
neurips-2025-dithub-a-modular-framework-.tldr: DitHub organizes detector adaptations as reusable expert branches that can be fetched and merged as specialized knowledge is needed.

paragraphs: Dr. RAW tackles high-level vision directly from camera RAW data while limiting how many model parameters must change for each task. It addresses two connected challenges: differences caused by sensors and illumination, and the expense of adapting a network separately for each application. The framework combines input normalization with lightweight task conditioning.

At the input stage, sensor and illumination mapping followed by re-mosaicing reduce inconsistencies in the data. Inside the network, Sensor Prior Prompts supply learnable conditioning based on imaging priors. Low-Rank Adaptation updates small matrix components in key backbone layers, enabling task-specific changes without fully fine-tuning the network. These mechanisms connect information about image formation with efficient adaptation.

The authors report superior results across object detection, semantic segmentation, instance segmentation, and pose estimation on nine datasets, including low-light and over-exposed conditions. The findings show that minimal parameter updates can deliver strong performance across the evaluated RAW tasks. They also support treating sensor-aware preparation and efficient network tuning as complementary parts of one vision framework.
neurips-2025-dr-raw-towards-general-high.tldr: Dr. RAW combines sensor-aware preprocessing, prompts, and low-rank adaptation for strong performance on multiple RAW vision tasks with minimal tuning.

paragraphs: Image fusion combines complementary information from images captured through different modalities. Diffusion-based approaches can produce strong results, but repeated sampling makes inference costly. RFfusion addresses this computational burden by using Rectified Flow to straighten the sampling trajectory, enabling one-step generation while maintaining high-quality fused images.

The framework also changes where fusion happens. A task-specific variational autoencoder combines source information in a latent representation, reducing computational complexity. Because a conventional autoencoder’s reconstruction objective does not fully match the requirements of fusion, the authors introduce two-stage training. This helps the model learn complementary source information while retaining fine structural detail.

The one-step sampling mechanism is described as requiring no additional training, while the overall framework includes its proposed two-stage training strategy. Experiments report better inference speed and fusion quality than other state-of-the-art methods. The contribution therefore combines a shorter generation procedure with a representation designed for fusion, addressing both the cost of sampling and the preservation of useful image information.
neurips-2025-efficient-rectified-flow-fo.tldr: RFfusion combines one-step Rectified Flow sampling with a fusion-specific latent representation to improve image-fusion speed and quality.

paragraphs: Federated continual learning must keep useful knowledge from earlier tasks while learning new tasks across clients. These goals are often described as stability and plasticity. MultiFCL builds on pretrained models, aiming to adapt their knowledge to this setting while retaining their generalization capabilities through a coordinated set of lightweight adaptation and knowledge-sharing mechanisms.

For stability, the framework learns task adapters and then freezes them to prevent catastrophic forgetting. It also uses semantic features from older tasks to initialize new class prototypes through multiple modalities. This gives new tasks a starting representation informed by previous knowledge while protecting the learned adapters associated with earlier tasks.

For plasticity, MultiFCL combines learning at multiple feature scales with dynamic self-distillation from multiple teachers. Experts communicate within and across clients, supporting knowledge fusion across both tasks and clients. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance across multiple datasets and settings. The findings support coordinating protected task-specific knowledge with active expert communication as an effective way to address the competing demands of federated continual learning.
neurips-2025-federated-continual-learnin.tldr: MultiFCL combines frozen task adapters with communicating experts to preserve old knowledge and learn new tasks across federated clients.

paragraphs: When evaluating a candidate solution is expensive, optimization must make productive use of a small number of evaluations. FSEO addresses this challenge for problems with multiple objectives. It uses experience from related optimization tasks to improve surrogate models, which help evolutionary algorithms decide how to search without evaluating every candidate directly.

The proposed surrogate combines a neural network with Gaussian processes. Network parameters and some Gaussian-process parameters represent experience shared across tasks and are meta-learned from related problems. Other Gaussian-process parameters remain specific to the target task. This division gives the model both reusable optimization knowledge and a way to represent features unique to the current problem.

The paper develops this architecture specifically for optimization and incorporates it into a generalized few-shot evolutionary framework. Its results demonstrate improved sampling efficiency for existing surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms on expensive multi-objective problems. The stated gain concerns using costly evaluations more effectively, with transfer from related tasks and target-specific modeling working together within the surrogate.
neurips-2025-fseo-few-shot-evolutionary-.tldr: FSEO meta-learns neural-network and Gaussian-process surrogates to improve evaluation efficiency in expensive multi-objective evolutionary optimization.

paragraphs: Reward functions shape what reinforcement-learning policies learn to do. LaRes makes those functions part of the search process in a framework combining evolutionary methods and reinforcement learning. A language model generates a population of reward functions, evaluates their usefulness through the performance of the policies they guide, and then improves them.

To reuse experience efficiently, LaRes pools data from all policies in a shared buffer. Each experience carries rewards from all reward functions, and those rewards are relabeled when the functions change. This lets historical data remain useful as reward search progresses. A Thompson-sampling selection mechanism further improves interactions among elite candidates.

Changing rewards can destabilize policy learning, so LaRes includes reward scaling and parameter constraints to coordinate the two processes and prevent policy collapse. Across initialized and non-initialized settings, experiments report state-of-the-art sample efficiency and final performance against strong baselines. The findings support searching over reward design while explicitly managing data reuse and the effects of reward changes on policy training.
neurips-2025-lares-evolutionary-reinforc.tldr: LaRes uses language models to evolve reward functions while sharing and relabeling experience to improve reinforcement-learning efficiency.

paragraphs: Diffusion transformers can struggle when asked to generate images larger than those used in training. The paper identifies extrapolation of explicit positional encodings, such as RoPE, as a primary obstacle. LEDiT removes explicit positional encodings and instead uses the attention structure itself to provide information about position.

Its central mechanism is causal attention, which the authors demonstrate can implicitly encode global positional information that helps extrapolation. A locality enhancement module complements that broad information with fine-grained local detail. The two components address different spatial scales: the attention pattern supplies coarse global position, while the additional module captures nearby structure.

Experiments on conditional generation and text-to-image generation show support for up to fourfold resolution scaling, illustrated by moving from 256 by 256 pixels to 512 by 512 pixels. That example doubles each side and quadruples pixel count. LEDiT achieves better image quality than state-of-the-art length-extrapolation methods in these tests, supporting implicit positional information as a promising alternative for generating beyond training resolution.
neurips-2025-ledit-your-length-extrapola.tldr: LEDiT uses causal attention and local detail modeling instead of explicit positional encodings to generate images beyond its training resolution.

paragraphs: LightFair investigates bias originating in the text encoder of a text-to-image diffusion model. The authors observe that supposedly neutral text embeddings have uneven relationships to image embeddings associated with different attributes in CLIP space. They also find that the noise prediction network amplifies this imbalance, making the text representation a useful intervention point.

The method fine-tunes text embeddings using a collaborative distance constraint that balances their distances without auxiliary references. Focusing on the text encoder reduces the burden associated with adapting multiple model components or adding correction networks. Because debiasing can harm generation quality, LightFair also uses two-stage text-guided sampling to control when the debiased encoder influences generation.

Experiments demonstrate effectiveness and efficiency. On Stable Diffusion v1.5, the authors report state-of-the-art debiasing with one-quarter of the training burden and virtually unchanged sampling burden. The findings support a targeted intervention at the text encoder, paired with control over its use during sampling, as an efficient way to address the evaluated biases while managing generation quality.
neurips-2025-lightfair-towards-an-effici.tldr: LightFair debiases text embeddings and controls their influence during sampling, achieving strong reported fairness results with substantially less training.

paragraphs: Unsupervised domain generalization seeks representations that remain useful under changing data conditions without category labels during representation learning. A central difficulty is separating semantic meaning from other variations. This paper also removes reliance on domain labels, framing the goal as retaining sufficient semantic information while discarding information unrelated to meaning.

The authors formalize this as a Minimal Sufficient Semantic Representation. Sufficiency preserves semantic information shared across augmented views; minimality removes irrelevant information. Their information-theoretic analysis connects optimizing these objectives with reduced out-of-distribution risk. This gives the practical method a stated theoretical target beyond simply making representations similar across different views.

MS-UDG implements sufficiency through an InfoNCE-based objective. It promotes minimality through a semantic-variation disentanglement loss and a reconstruction mechanism that captures adequate variation. Experiments establish a new state of the art on popular UDG benchmarks, consistently exceeding existing self-supervised and UDG methods. These results support explicitly separating meaning and variation while learning without either category labels or domain labels.
neurips-2025-minimal-semantic-sufficienc.tldr: MS-UDG learns representations that preserve shared semantics and remove irrelevant variation, improving domain generalization without category or domain labels.

paragraphs: A feature can influence a model’s prediction without being dependent on the target outcome. Such suppressor variables can mislead explanation methods into assigning apparent importance where it does not reflect a relationship with the target. PatternLocal addresses this problem for nonlinear models and explanations of individual predictions, extending a concern already studied in linear models.

The method starts with a locally linear approximation, such as one produced by LIME, KernelSHAP, or a gradient-based approach. It then transforms the approximation’s discriminative weights into a generative representation. This transformation is designed to suppress the contribution of suppressor variables while preserving local fidelity, keeping the explanation connected to the model’s behavior near the instance.

Following extensive hyperparameter optimization on XAI-TRIS, PatternLocal consistently outperforms other explanation methods and reduces false-positive attributions on nonlinear tasks. An additional EEG motor-imagery evaluation produces physiologically plausible explanations. These findings support correcting local attribution weights as a way to improve explanation reliability, with evidence from both a benchmark and a physiological application.
neurips-2025-minimizing-false-positive-a.tldr: PatternLocal transforms local explanation weights to reduce misleading attributions from suppressor variables while preserving local fidelity.

paragraphs: Partially relevant video retrieval finds videos containing a segment that matches a text query. Standard training can distort meaning by treating all annotated pairs as positives and every other pairing as negative. Distinct events within one video can become too similar in representation, while similar events across different videos are pushed apart.

The proposed framework addresses this semantic collapse in both text and video representations. Text Correlation Preservation Learning retains relationships among queries already encoded by a foundation model. Cross-Branch Video Alignment uses contrastive alignment to separate hierarchical video representations across temporal scales, helping preserve differences between the events represented at those scales.

Order-preserving token merging and adaptive alignment further produce segments that are coherent internally but distinguishable from one another. Experiments on PRVR benchmarks show prevention of semantic collapse and substantial improvements in retrieval accuracy. The contribution is to make training respect the semantic diversity inside videos and the similarities that can cross video boundaries, rather than letting pair annotations alone determine those relationships.
neurips-2025-mitigating-semantic-collaps.tldr: The framework improves partially relevant video retrieval by preserving semantic relationships among queries and distinct events within video representations.

paragraphs: Vision backbones typically reduce spatial resolution through uniform downsampling. This paper replaces that fixed spatial reduction with a content-aware grouping layer. The layer assigns image tokens to a smaller set according to image boundaries and semantic content, allowing the way information is compressed to reflect the structure of the image itself.

Stacking these layers across consecutive backbone stages produces hierarchical segmentation during feature extraction. The resulting architecture is called a Native Segmentation Vision Transformer because segmentation emerges within the backbone. With careful architectural design, the grouping layers themselves produce strong masks, without requiring an additional segmentation-specific head to turn features into segments.

The authors report strong zero-shot results without mask supervision and an efficient, minimal standalone design for downstream segmentation tasks. These findings support treating spatial grouping as more than a way to reduce computation: it can also organize image content into meaningful regions. The contribution links resolution reduction and segmentation within the same architectural operation, with groups formed at successive levels of the backbone.
neurips-2025-native-segmentation-vision-.tldr: Content-aware token grouping lets vision transformers produce segmentation masks directly within their backbones, including zero-shot results without mask supervision.

paragraphs: Machine unlearning aims to remove unwanted knowledge from a pretrained model without retraining it completely. This paper finds that apparent success on ordinary benchmarks can conceal unintended losses of benign knowledge. The authors call these losses knowledge holes: questions the original model could answer may receive irrelevant or nonsensical responses after unlearning.

To locate these failures, they develop a framework that generates targeted test cases. It examines both content close to what was deliberately removed and broader regions where failures might occur. This approach probes preservation more actively than a fixed benchmark, searching for damage that aggregate performance on standard tests can miss.

In the reported evaluation, up to 98.7% of generated test cases produce irrelevant or nonsensical answers from unlearned models despite being answerable by the pretrained model. This figure describes the tested cases, rather than all possible benign questions. The findings show why evaluating knowledge preservation requires attention to targeted failure regions, even when standard benchmark performance appears largely intact.
neurips-2025-probing-hidden-knowledge-ho.tldr: Targeted tests reveal that machine unlearning can erase benign knowledge in ways that standard benchmarks fail to detect.

paragraphs: Dynamic graph models must represent both connections and how interactions unfold over time. Memory-based approaches capture short-range patterns well, but can struggle with distant dependencies and the integration of graph structure. SALoM addresses these problems through a memory design that combines information across different time scales with structural signals.

Its memory module tackles vanishing gradients and information forgetting to retain longer-term dependencies. A long-short memory updater dynamically balances recent and distant correlations, aiming to prevent over-generalization. This balance matters because retaining older information alone does not determine how strongly it should influence a prediction relative to more recent activity.

SALoM combines the updater with co-occurrence encoding through an information-bottleneck-based fusion mechanism, bringing temporal and structural information together. Experiments across multiple graph datasets report state-of-the-art dynamic link prediction performance. The findings support treating long-term retention, short-term adaptation, and structural integration as coordinated parts of the model, rather than expecting a single undifferentiated memory to handle all three demands.
neurips-2025-salom-structure-aware-tempo.tldr: SALoM improves dynamic graph link prediction by balancing long- and short-term memory and fusing it with structural information.

paragraphs: Spatio-temporal video grounding identifies where a text-described target appears and the time interval in which it appears. This paper develops a zero-shot approach using multimodal language models. The authors observe that these models dynamically use particular tokens for grounding, but often fail to combine all the attributes and actions expressed in a query.

Their decomposed spatio-temporal highlighting strategy splits the query into attribute and action subqueries. A logit-guided re-attention module learns latent spatial and temporal prompts by regularizing token predictions for those subqueries. The prompts emphasize relevant appearance and action cues, helping direct attention toward visual regions useful for locating the target in space and time.

A temporal-augmented assembling strategy then combines predictions from original and temporally augmented frames to improve consistency over time. Evaluations across different multimodal language models outperform state-of-the-art methods on three common benchmarks. The findings support separating complementary query cues and then assembling consistent predictions as a way to better use these models’ existing grounding and reasoning abilities.
neurips-2025-unleashing-the-potential-of.tldr: Separating attribute and action cues helps multimodal language models locate text-described targets more accurately and consistently across video frames.

paragraphs: Contextual bandit algorithms choose actions using available context and learn from noisy rewards. Variance-dependent regret bounds describe performance in a way that reflects the amount of reward noise. This paper extends such analysis for Thompson sampling, where earlier variance-aware work was limited to linear rewards and had suboptimal dependence on model dimension.

The proposed FGTS-VA algorithm handles general reward functions. Its analysis extends the decoupling coefficient used in Feel-Good Thompson Sampling to represent model-space complexity. The regret bound scales, up to logarithmic factors, with the square root of that coefficient times the logarithm of model-space size times cumulative noise scale, plus an additive complexity term.

The noise quantity is expressed through a subgaussian parameter and corresponds to variance for Gaussian noise. Thus, the guarantee explicitly accounts for noise accumulated over the interaction rounds. For contextual linear bandits, the bound matches weighted-linear-regression UCB methods. This establishes a sampling-based route to the stated optimal regret guarantee while extending the reward-function setting beyond the earlier linear-only approach.
neurips-2025-variance-aware-feel-good-th.tldr: FGTS-VA gives variance-aware Thompson sampling regret guarantees for general reward functions and matches established UCB bounds in linear contextual bandits.

paragraphs: HeisenVec is a dataset for generating vector graphics from natural-language descriptions. Its focus is SVG, where an image is represented by drawing commands and styling information. This makes generation a structured sequence problem: the output must describe graphic elements symbolically, bringing language modeling into direct contact with the representation used for vector images.

The dataset contains 2.2 million SVGs collected from online sources, each paired with four complementary descriptions generated by multimodal models. A preprocessing pipeline converts geometric primitives into paths, applies affine transformations, and compresses the syntax with custom tokens. These steps standardize the graphics and make their sequences more consistent for autoregressive modeling.

HeisenVec covers varied visual styles and sequence lengths, with a substantial share of examples longer than 8,000 tokens. That makes it useful for evaluating long-context models as well as text-conditioned SVG generation. The authors release the dataset, tokenization tools, and evaluation pipeline, providing a common foundation for investigating how language models produce long, structured graphical outputs.
neurips-2025-vhector-and-heisenvec-scala.tldr: HeisenVec provides 2.2 million standardized SVGs with textual descriptions and evaluation tools for language-driven vector graphics generation.

paragraphs: Videos of the same event recorded by different cameras can start at different times, making synchronization difficult. VisualSync estimates these time offsets from object motion across views. It targets videos that are both unsynchronized and unposed, using visual evidence to align streams whose camera relationships are not supplied in advance.

The key geometric observation concerns a moving 3D point visible in two cameras: at the correct synchronization, its projections satisfy epipolar constraints. VisualSync uses existing 3D reconstruction, feature matching, and dense tracking methods to obtain short tracks, relative camera poses, and cross-view correspondences. It then jointly estimates camera time offsets by minimizing the associated epipolar error.

Experiments on four diverse, challenging datasets show better synchronization than baseline methods, with average error below 130 milliseconds. The reported evidence supports motion-based geometric alignment across the tested settings. Shared visibility of moving points is central to the method’s reasoning, because those cross-view observations provide the constraints that connect camera timing to geometric consistency.
neurips-2025-visual-sync-multicamera-syn.tldr: VisualSync synchronizes unposed camera videos through cross-view motion geometry, reporting average error below 130 milliseconds across four datasets.
